title: Residency-aware retention automations and verifiable deletion manifests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver an automated retention execution engine that enforces tenant and region-specific retention windows, performs safe deletion workflows, and emits verifiable deletion manifests (signed, tamper-evident bundles) customers can retrieve as proof of compliance. The feature must support scheduled purges, on-demand RTBF requests, dry-run validation, and a lightweight evidence export format consumable by downstream GRC tooling.
acceptance_criteria: Retention engine applies tenant-scoped and region-scoped TTLs and respects per-tenant overrides
Scheduled purge jobs execute without breaching SLOs for live inference (defined as <2% increase in p99 latency during purge windows)
On-demand RTBF request endpoint triggers deletion workflow and returns a signed manifest URL within SLA (24h for pilot tenants)
Deletion manifests include immutable event IDs, deletion timestamps, deleted object counts, cryptographic signature (service signing key), and Merkle root of deleted object identifiers
Dry-run mode produces a preview manifest without performing deletions and is accessible via console and API
Evidence export ZIP is verifiable offline and includes a manifest, audit log segment, and signature bundle
E2E tests and an integration smoke test against the retention simulator exist in CI and pass in the privacy-2026.04 release pipeline
success_metrics: Pilot tenant RTBF SLA met for 95% of requests within 24 hours
Zero customer complaints related to inadvertent cross-region deletions after rollout
Deletion manifests served and verifiable for 100% of completed deletion runs in pilot
No more than 2% p99 latency uplift during scheduled purge maintenance windows in Dedicated clusters
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Dry-run & simulator (internal): enable retention engine in dry-run across test tenants, validate manifests with simulator datasets
Phase 2 - Pilot tenants: opt-in pilot with two enterprise customers in different geozones; provide manual evidence exports and runbooks
Phase 3 - Gradual rollout: enable scheduled purges for low-traffic accounts, monitor latency/cost signals, enable auto-scaling of purge workers
Phase 4 - GA: enable self-serve RTBF requests in console, provide webhook/callback for manifest delivery and tenant-facing download link
design_decisions: Use append-only event store for deletion events to support efficient evidence extraction and replay
Emit signed manifests (ECDSA) with Merkle root of identifiers to balance payload size and tamper-evidence
Perform deletions asynchronously with strong eventual consistency to avoid synchronous latency penalties on inference API
Provide a dry-run mode to mitigate accidental policy misconfigurations and give customers preview evidence
Retention simulator integration to estimate cost and expected object churn before enabling deletes in a tenant
tradeoffs: Synchronous deletion provides stronger immediate guarantees but would increase API latencies — chosen async deletions to protect inference SLOs
Merkle-based manifests reduce transmitted data but require customers to retain their identifier lists for independent verification
Keeping an append-only deletion store improves auditability but requires retention of minimal metadata for the audit window; must balance retention of metadata vs privacy
Signing manifests increases operational key management needs (rotate keys, KMS/HSM integration)
